subject: Discovery recap: throughput fit & reserved GPU proposal
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <leah@calypso-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: throughput fit & reserved GPU proposal

Hi Leah — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so everyone is aligned. Let me know if I mischaracterized anything.

What we heard (pain points)
- Latency spikes during your 10:00–12:00 UTC window; p95 regularly exceeding 1.2s under peak.
- Current k8s/Triton multi-tenant setup is noisy: resource contention during batch jobs and model warm-up issues.
- Unpredictable spend and occasional evictions from shared pools when you hit burst traffic.

Goals / success criteria
- Sustained inference throughput target: ~500 requests/sec (average) with bursts to ~1,200 rps for 5–15 minutes.
- P50 latency target < 120ms; p95 < 400ms for 512-token requests.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools (no co-tenancy) and customer-side KMS for keys.
- Ops: 99.9% availability for inference endpoints and automated rollback on degradations.

Current stack (as you described)
- Models served on internal Triton cluster, fronted by an API mesh.
- Redis for KV cache; logs forwarded to Splunk.
- CI deploys nightly; no formal canary for model rollouts today.

Initial Dedicated fit guidance (what Redwood proposes)
- Reserved pool: baseline of 4xA100-equivalent instances (prelim estimate in attached sizing workbook) with 2x burst nodes in a separate burst pool.
- Autoscaling policy: continuous batching + latency SLO target per node; burst pool to scale by CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth.
- Network/isolation: VPC peering and optional Private deployment if you need on-prem networking.

Open questions we need you to confirm
1) Typical request token length distribution (mean and 95th). We asked for a short traffic sample — can you attach or confirm?
2) Burst profile confirmation: 1,200 rps for 10–15 minutes is what we recorded today; please confirm worst-case.
3) Data residency / retention limits and whether SOC2 evidence must be provided before procurement.

Next steps / asks
- Leah: please attach a 24–72 hour traffic sample (CSV) and confirm burst duration.
- Redwood (Markus/Monica/Vivek): prepare a tech deep-dive focused on baseline config, steady-state sizing, and canary plan.
- Schedule: propose Tue 12 May, 10:00 PT for a 60-minute tech deep-dive + ops Q&A.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-model.xlsx (prelim), SOC2 checklist (redwood).

Thanks — I’ll circulate a short M.A.P. (mutual action plan) after we confirm the above.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference platform
From: Leah Park <leah@calypso-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, procurement@calypso-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: throughput fit & reserved GPU proposal

Thanks Markus — this aligns well. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

Confirmed numbers
- Sustained baseline: 500 rps average during business hours (US/EU).
- Burst: we commonly see spikes up to 1,200 rps for 8–12 minutes; very occasionally up to ~1,500 rps for <3 minutes (during external campaign traffic).
- Token length: median ~180 tokens, 95th ~640 tokens; attached is a 48-hour sample (calypso-traffic-sample.csv).

Security / compliance
- SOC2 is a procurement requirement; we need a completed questionnaire and evidence before final sign-off. Retention policy: customer PII must be retained for no more than 30 days by default.
- We require that inference logs that contain user prompts be optional and encrypted; customer-managed KMS preferred.

Procurement timeline & constraints
- Procurement window is ~8–10 weeks once we agree on SOW and pricing.
- We have an internal requirement to review any platform-level audit logs for a 30-day window.

Operational note
- Canary/cutover: we prefer a two-week canary with progressively increasing traffic to the reserved pool (10% → 40% → 100%).

Happy to meet Tue 12 May 10:00 PT. Monica — FYI on procurement cadence and SOC2 ask.

Leah Park
Head of Infrastructure — Calypso Analytics
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: throughput fit & reserved GPU proposal

Markus / Vivek — forwarding Leah’s confirmations. Quick internal notes and proposed approach:

- Preliminary config: 4xA100 baseline in reserved pool + 2xA100 burst (separate pool) should cover sustained 500 rps and short bursts to 1,200 rps assuming batching and KV cache hit ~30%. Sizing details in redwood-sizing-model.xlsx.
- Autoscaling: use dual-trigger policy (GPU util > 70% OR request queue depth > 150) with cooldown windows to prevent oscillation.
- Canary plan: follow Leah’s 2-week ramp; implement traffic-splitting with fallback to hosted small model variant if degradation detected.
- Risks: if their 95th token length varies upward (e.g., >800 tokens) we need +1 node baseline. Add as contingency line item for SOW.

Action items for internal owners
- Vivek: draft baseline runbook (latency SLOs, rollback triggers, monitoring dashboards).
- Markus: draft mutual action plan & preliminary SOW + proposed pricing/disc for reserved capacity.
- Monica: compile SOC2 evidence checklist and match to procurement ask — share with Leah.

Can we meet Mon 11 May 09:00 PT for 30m internal sync before the tech deep-dive?

--Monica
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <leah@calypso-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: throughput fit & reserved GPU proposal

Thanks all — appreciate the quick confirmations, Leah. Finalizing logistics below: 

1) Tech deep-dive: Tue 12 May, 10:00 PT (60 min). Agenda: measured baseline vs. sample traffic, proposed reserved pool sizing, canary plan and rollback conditions, security controls (KMS + audit logs).
2) Pre-reads: I shared the sizing workbook and a short runbook draft to the Drive folder (link below). Please review the sizing tab and the assumptions section before the call.
3) SOC2: Monica will send the completed checklist and the relevant attachments by EOD Mon so procurement can review.
4) M.A.P & SOW: I’ll circulate a mutual action plan right after the deep-dive. Expect a draft SOW and pricing (including a reserved-capacity credit proposal) within 3 business days after the call.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-model.xlsx (attached), SOC2-questions-calypso.pdf (copy).

DocuSign link for an NDA/provisional SOW will be shared if procurement requests it: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123

Thanks — see you on Tue.

Best,
Markus
